unit.why: A first-person memorate quoted from Zohar Hai: the author describes how his holy teachers and his uncle spoke only in yihudim even in worldly talk, and how his uncle repeatedly sent him away so as not to disturb the salvation being drawn down.

stories.start_quote: בזהר חי פ׳ ויחי בדפי הספר
stories.summary_en: The author of Zohar Hai recalls that his teachers' every word, even worldly stories, held yihudim and holy names, and that his uncle asked him several times to leave because his understanding of those yihudim hindered the salvation the uncle was drawing down for a petitioner.

quotes: שכל דיבורם הי' ביחודים ושמות ומוסר ודרכי היחוד
tags.why: The tzaddikim's speech performs mystical unifications

quotes: שכל דיבורם הי' ביחודים ושמות ומוסר ודרכי היחוד
tags.why: Contemplative yihudim performed within ordinary speech

quotes: אף שהיו מספרים סיפורי מעשיות ועניני צרכי הגוף
tags.why: Telling stories is shown as a vehicle for yihudim, a theurgic act

quotes: ממה שצריך להמשיך ישועה של אותו הנצרך לישועה
tags.why: The tzaddik's speech draws down salvation for those in need

quotes: מדבר עם האנשים הנצרכים לכמה ענינים מעניני עוה״ז
tags.why: The uncle receives people who come with worldly needs

quotes: וכמעט הייתי נרתע באימה מגודל האור והחכמה
tags.why: The author is struck with awe at his teachers' words
Recoiling in dread, though mainly awe

quotes: וכ״פ ביקש ממני שאלך ולא אשמע
tags.why: The narrator is the disciple of his uncle and teacher

quotes: הי׳ מדבר דברים נפלאים ושכליות רמות סודות נשגבות
tags.why: Hidden mystical meanings lie within worldly speech

quotes: כי מחמת שאנכי מבין מעניני היחודים של דיבוריו
tags.why: The disciple perceives the hidden yihudim others miss
The tale shows the holiness of the masters' speech
